sections.intent: State the heavy Yaman mukhada over a galloping mid-tempo metal groove
sections.transition: Rhythm guitar accents sam and thickens tone for the takeover

sections.intent: Guitar takes over the mukhada theme with crushing palm-muted chugs and power chords
sections.transition: Snare roll launches the sitar into the climactic taan

sections.intent: Virtuosic chaugun taan climbing through madhya saptak to taar Sa and cascading down
sections.transition: Descending run hits the sam of the final mukhada with absolute impact

sections.intent: Final triumphant return of the mukhada resolving to sam on low Sa
sections.transition: Crushing final hit on sam with instant silence

request: a one-minute heavy metal song in raga Yaman, key of E, 128 bpm

seed_riff.reasoning: A driving 16-matra Teentaal riff built on Yaman's N-R-G-M-P framework. Root notes land heavily on sam (S) and tali (G on beat 5, N on beat 13), using tight palm-muted gallops and open breathing rests on beats 8 and 12.

phrase_plan.climax_and_sam: Peaks on Pa in the response, resolves through mandra Ni to land squarely on sam Sa

seed_head.idea: Heavy Yaman mukhada ascending N-R-G to vadi G, dipping through tivra Ma to Pa, and resolving via G-R-S onto sam Sa

energy_arc: mukhada: medium-heavy groove establishing the Yaman theme with authoritative drive; takeover: explosive rhythmic crunch with low power-chord chugs taking the lead; taan_long: maximum blistering energy with driven chaugun sitar runs peaking at taar Sa; mukhada: powerful anthemic reprise slamming tightly into the final sam.

rhythm_section.reasoning: Raga Yaman heavy metal arrangement at 128 bpm in Teentaal (16 beats). For Section 0 (mukhada), establish an authoritative mid-tempo NWOBHM gallop and power-chord drive following the harmonic scheme: S power (beats 0-7), G power (beats 8-11), P power (beats 12-15). Section 1 is a takeover section, which by rule is handled by code arranging the guitar from the realized mukhada, so no part is written for it. For Section 2 (taan_long), lock into an unrelenting pedal-point chug on Sa (S) to provide an unyielding rhythmic floor beneath the sitar's rapid chaugun taan runs. For Section 3 (final mukhada), provide an anthemic return matching the harmony plan (S power 12, N power 2, S power 2) with massive ringing accents on sam.

parts.role: Mukhada groove: tight galloping rhythm guitar anchoring low Sa, moving to Ga and Pa power chords, leaving space for sitar flourishes
High-octane driving pedal beneath virtuosic chaugun taan: continuous 8th and 16th gallops on root Sa driving to Taar Sa climax
Final triumphant mukhada reprise: heavy S power foundation moving through N leading tone into an authoritative sam resolution
